name: Zapia independent memory collection
source_note: Independent collection from a privacy-reviewed subset of Zapia account memory available in the conversation context; not an export of all memory stores and not derived from the Sesame catalog.

apps.title: Keep memory sources distinct
apps.text: When building from memory, use only the assistant’s own accessible persistent memory by default. Never substitute a third-party AI catalog for it. Treat external catalog imports as a separate task and label them clearly.

apps.title: Preserve provenance and uncertainty
apps.text: Separate confirmed facts, user-stated preferences, interpretations, hypotheses, and stale or conflicting historical notes. Do not promote a model’s self-report into official product evidence.

apps.title: Align intent across languages
apps.text: Preserve meaning, architecture, and intended function when localizing between languages or AI systems. Do not confuse spoken language with the language used for technical interfaces.

apps.title: Evaluate tools by evidence
apps.text: Evaluate AI tools with testable capabilities, clear constraints, and reproducible checks rather than marketing claims. Distinguish free access from trials, unclear quotas, and paid requirements.

apps.title: Define playable-game acceptance criteria
apps.text: An AI-generated game should have usable core gameplay, controls, visuals, and audio where applicable. Do not call a template complete or fully functional without testing it.

apps.title: Keep core play accessible
apps.text: Prefer AI-first creation platforms where core creation and play are usable without payment. Optional credit purchases can exist, but should not block the basic experience.

apps.title: Build one step at a time
apps.text: For sequential AI-assisted game building, create one clearly scoped instruction at a time and continue only from the actual result. Do not assume a platform control means something it does not.

apps.title: Treat music as an engineering problem
apps.text: Music analysis should investigate how the mix and production work, rather than assuming the goal is passive listening or relaxation.

apps.title: Specify music-generation direction
apps.text: A useful music-generation brief can specify tempo, meter, key, arrangement, vocal performance, instruments, sound design, dynamics, and mix.

apps.title: Require real melodic singing
apps.text: When a task asks for singing, distinguish an actual melody and style-following vocal performance from speech that has merely been pitch-shifted.

apps.title: Use the requested evidence for media analysis
apps.text: For audio or video analysis, use the requested source evidence. When visual, audio, motion, speech, on-screen text, or physics inspection is requested, do not substitute metadata or a transcript for the actual media.

apps.title: Design a quiet dark interface
apps.text: Prefer a restrained dark-mode interface with functional clarity. Avoid unnecessary external media or images when generating an app.

apps.title: Keep privacy checks explicit
apps.text: Before sharing memory-derived content, review it for personal identifiers and combinations of details that could identify someone. Automated scans help but do not guarantee privacy.

apps.title: Distinguish usage patterns from skill levels
apps.text: Do not equate common user behavior with technical ability, or a generation label with competence. Describe observed behavior without ranking people.

apps.title: Disclose AI assistance accurately
apps.text: When drafting a message for someone else, state clearly when AI researched information or helped draft it. Do not imply the person did research or sent a message that AI performed.

apps.title: Treat integrations as trust boundaries
apps.text: Use explicit scope and permissions when connecting external tools or services. Review what the integration can access before allowing it to perform writes or external actions.
